close_reason: Landed in b091273 as side-effect of JMAP-t307.1. The bench file's module-level doc comment was rewritten as part of the t307.1 refactor: it now explicitly describes the two-layer guarantee ('Fixture builders and structural-invariant asserts live in tests/common/mod.rs and are shared with tests/bench_fixtures.rs so that the structural invariants run under cargo test (the workspace pre-commit gate) and not only under cargo bench. The asserts here at fixture-setup time are belt-and-suspenders...'). The misleading 'equivalent guarantee' phrasing is gone.
description:
What is unclear and for whom: crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:199-202 says 'Bench targets use harness = false, so #[test] items inside this file would never be collected; inline assertions are the equivalent guarantee.' A future contributor reading this will conclude that the bench-internal asserts are CI-checked. They are not — see sibling P1 finding JMAP-t307.1 — because cargo bench is not in the pre-commit gate.

The reader who follows this misleading claim will (a) not write a separate fixture-shape test when they extend the bench file, and (b) believe that breaking a fixture will be caught by CI when it will not.

Fix: rewrite the comment to say what is actually true: 'Asserted once per bench function during fixture setup. Note: these asserts only execute when the bench runs under cargo bench, which is not in the workspace pre-commit gate. A breakage in a fixture's structural invariant will not be caught by cargo test --workspace. See tests/bench_fixtures.rs for the test-gated equivalents.' (assuming JMAP-t307.1 lands the test-gated equivalents).

If the sibling P1 finding is rejected and asserts remain bench-only, then the comment should at least drop the false 'equivalent guarantee' phrasing.
title: Bench doc comment claims fixture asserts are 'equivalent guarantee' to #[test]
